title: MSFS 2024 just got a massive scenery upgrade! (World Update 22 & New Releases)
description:
The Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 marketplace just exploded with an incredibly diverse set of releases this week, bringing a massive mix of high-fidelity international airliner hubs, unique regional fields, and stunning visual landmarks. Whether you enjoy challenging, low-visibility long-haul airliner routes, low-level VFR flying over hidden backcountry airfields, or upgrading your dark-hour atmosphere, this week's drop covers an incredible amount of ground.

In this comprehensive marketplace breakdown, we are putting the biggest new releases head-to-head against the default MSFS 2024 streaming engine to analyze the structural upgrades, terminal interior details, and night illumination overhauls to see which add-ons genuinely deserve a spot in your virtual hangar.

To make sense of this massive drop, we have organized the latest releases into three logical categories:

✈️ SCENIC HOLIDAY & REGIONAL GATEWAYS: We kick off with the heavy seasonal holiday routes, heading straight to Corfu International Airport (LGKR) by Gaya Simulations. We evaluate its terminal realism, interior modeling, and night lighting before running a side-by-side comparison against the default MSFS 2024 engine. Next, we journey to Colombia to check out Olaya Herrera Airport (SKMD) by Cheros Sim Solutions to analyze its custom terminal interiors, unique slope runway, and city landmarks.

⛰️ RUGGED BACKCOUNTRY & SMALL REGIONAL AIRSTRIPS: For the bush pilots, we dive into a challenging two-in-one package featuring Idaho's Mahoney Creek Airstrip (O03) and the ultra-short Cougar Range Airfield (D47), assessing their custom PBR textures and demanding plateau approaches. We then head down to Brazil to check out Aeroparque Aldeia da Serra (SJOY) by Flyt, running a default comparison to show how this executive aviation community is completely transformed.

🏞️ FIRST-PARTY WORLD EXPANSIONS: Finally, we unpack the massive, free World Update 22: United States National Parks expansion. Developed alongside Bing Places, Vexcel, Gaya, and Asobo, this immense package overhauls 31 areas of interest with updated photogrammetry, irregular network surfaces, and 46 stunning points of interest. We break down the natural wonders from Arches and Zion to Death Valley, and take a look at the brand-new activity type: Guided Tours!

Are you going to be taking a commercial ride to the Greek islands, practicing your short-field backcountry arrivals at Mahoney Creek, or exploring the new national parks? Let me know in the comments below: which of these packages is landing on your hard drive first?

If this structured marketplace breakdown helps you plan your next flight route, make sure to hit that like button and subscribe for weekly MSFS realism updates!

(Stay tuned to the channel as I'll soon be sharing my first VR flight experience inside MSFS 2024 using the Pimax Crystal Light!)
